description: Four verified microscope and physical-science source observations with license and image-processing disclosures.

images.title: An analog oscilloscope shows changing voltage
images.summary: An Esselte Type D-5 oscilloscope photographed on 20 December 2023 displays a blue trace across its cathode-ray-tube screen. An oscilloscope maps electrical signal voltage against time.
images.alt: Beige analog oscilloscope with control knobs and a blue oscillating voltage trace on the gridded central screen.
images.caption: A real oscilloscope displaying a changing electrical signal. The horizontal axis represents elapsed time at a user-selected scale; vertical deflection corresponds to voltage.
images.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication by Unnerving duck, documented at https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Esselte_oscilloscope.jpg .
images.processing: Resized from the Commons source JPEG to maximum 1800 pixels and re-encoded at JPEG quality 87 for the development archive; no synthetic content.

images.title: Real samples of chemical elements arranged in a periodic table
images.summary: A physical acrylic display contains selected actual element specimens arranged by atomic number, with labels and symbols. It was photographed by Achituv in October 2020.
images.alt: Grid of individually labeled acrylic element display blocks across a large pale background, with some blocks containing visible metal or mineral samples.
images.caption: A human-created physical periodic-table display contains many element samples. Some hazardous, unstable or gaseous elements are represented by symbols or empty blocks rather than loose specimens. The written labels are not a self-decoding alien primer.
images.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 International (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Original photograph by Achituv; edited development JPEG derivative is also CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution and modification indicated.
images.processing: Original Commons photograph (perspective-corrected 2022 version) downsampled to maximum 1800px and encoded at JPEG quality 87; attribution retained.

images.title: Ice crystals revealed in polarized light
images.summary: A real polarized-light microscopy image of ice crystals growing in ice cream after six months in storage; the sample contained added antifreeze protein. The geometric crystalline structures are physically observed.
images.alt: Bright microscopic crystalline geometric forms in several vivid polarized-light interference colors.
images.caption: Microscopy of actual frozen-water crystals in an ice-cream sample. The false-looking vivid interference colors arise from crossed polarization and are not the naked-eye colors of ice.
images.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 International (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Photograph © Maxim Bilovitskiy; resized and re-encoded derivative shared under same license.
images.processing: Source 6000x4000 polarized-light image reduced to maximum 1800px and quality-87 JPEG; optical colors preserved, no generated image.

images.title: Diamond and graphite: two forms of carbon
images.summary: Two separate mineral specimen photographs by Rob Lavinsky are displayed together in a Commons comparative composite edited by Jynto. Diamond and graphite have the same chemical element but different crystal arrangements.
images.alt: A small translucent octahedral diamond crystal on the left and a dark black lustrous graphite mineral fragment on the right, against a white background.
images.caption: Diamond (left) and graphite (right) are both carbon but have different atomic structures and properties. This is a photographic composite of different specimens; the two objects are not shown at one reliable physical scale.
images.credit: Rob Lavinsky / iRocks.com; comparison composite edited by Jynto
images.rights: CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). © Rob Lavinsky / iRocks.com, composite by Jynto; re-encoded derivative shared under compatible CC BY-SA 3.0 with credit and modification notice.
images.processing: Photographic comparison assembled from two mineral photos by Jynto; scale is approximate. Development image locally re-encoded quality-87, not AI-generated.
